headline: Google AI Studio now supports Next.js for app building
summary: The updated app-building experience in Google AI Studio now offers support for Next.js, React, and Angular, aiming to streamline development with an enhanced coding agent.
details: Google AI Studio has updated its app-building experience to include support for Next.js, React, and Angular. This enhancement aims to provide developers with a more efficient workflow for creating applications.

The platform features a coding agent that reportedly maintains a deeper understanding of project structure and chat history. This is intended to facilitate faster iteration and more precise multi-step code edits for developers.

Key features highlighted include secure API-key storage, connections to various services, and the ability to integrate databases and multiplayer functionality, making it a comprehensive tool for app development.

While Google AI Studio's capabilities are geared towards building apps, the article emphasizes that this does not automatically mean a generated application is production-ready. Developers are advised to verify implementations independently.

The guide focuses on the verified Next.js workflow, noting that developers can select this framework in the updated Settings panel. The source does not specify exact implementation steps or menu names, encouraging users to check the current product interface.

The article stresses the importance of planning a clearly scoped application idea and understanding the difference between a generated interface, a connected service, and a deployable production system.

headline_marked: YouTube Music [[adds new labels]] for AI-generated songs
headline: YouTube Music adds new labels for AI-generated songs
summary: Listeners can now easily identify tracks created with AI, with labels appearing on the player page for full transparency.
details: YouTube Music announced Wednesday the rollout of a new labeling system aimed at improving transparency around songs created with the help of generative AI. Now, listeners will be able to easily identify tracks created using AI, including those involved in composition and vocals.

The label will appear on the player page. Clicking on this label provides additional information about the specific role of AI in the track’s creation. Notably, these labels will also extend to the main YouTube app.

YouTube said it collaborated with various music partners and deployed its own detection tools to identify AI-generated music. Partners using YouTube can declare their work’s use of generative AI through three designations: “Fully Gen AI,” “Partly Gen AI,” or “No Gen AI.”

“Fully Gen AI” applies to tracks that are entirely generated by AI, while “Partly Gen AI” refers to works where artists may have incorporated AI-generated components but added their own live elements. Tracks edited using pitch-correction tools such as Auto-Tune fall under the “No Gen AI” category.

The move comes as AI-generated music rapidly expands across streaming services, with platforms like Apple Music, Spotify, Deezer, and TIDAL also adopting their own approaches to labeling and managing AI content.

YouTube, by contrast, is focusing on disclosure rather than blanket restrictions. Its new labels are intended to inform listeners about AI’s role in music creation, but AI involvement alone doesn’t make a track ineligible for monetization. YouTube even experiments with AI-powered music creation, including its tool Dream Track.
